title: SignalEvent
description: An async notification emitted by research-openclaw or subconscious-openclaw to workspace/research-vault/signals/ when a finding, contradiction, or pattern warrants Hermes attention outside the normal review cycle. Hermes polls this directory after each worker callback and routes signal events into its planning loop. Signal events are informational — they advise Hermes but do not trigger automatic action.

run_id.description: run_id of the job that produced this signal.

signal_type.description: Categorical type of signal. Hermes uses this to route the signal into the appropriate planning branch.

severity.description: 'critical' and 'high' signals are surfaced to the human operator immediately. 'medium' and below are queued for the next planning cycle.

summary.description: Plain-language description of what was detected and why it matters. Must be standalone-readable by Hermes without access to the underlying finding or walk record.

evidence.description: Cross-references to the artifacts that grounded this signal.

recommended_action.description: Worker's recommended next action for Hermes. Hermes decides whether to act — this is advisory only.

context.description: Optional structured context to help Hermes act on the recommendation.

suggested_objective.description: Draft objective text Hermes can use as-is or adapt for a follow-up broker job.

cve_id.description: CVE identifier if signal_type is cve_detected.

acknowledged.description: Set to true by Hermes after processing this signal. Unacknowledged signals are re-surfaced each planning cycle.

hermes_action_taken.description: Written by Hermes describing what action was taken in response to this signal.

expires_at.description: Optional TTL after which this signal is auto-archived if unacknowledged. Useful for informational/low signals that become stale.

examples.title: W3C Trace Context Level 2 deprecates baggage header forwarding requirements
examples.summary: A new finding indicates that the W3C Trace Context Level 2 working draft has removed the MUST-forward requirement for baggage headers in async contexts. This contradicts finding f1a2b3c4 and may require updates to the broker job payload spec and worker span propagation logic.

context.suggested_objective: Fetch and verify the W3C Trace Context Level 2 working draft. Confirm whether baggage forwarding requirements have changed. Update finding f1a2b3c4 if confirmed.
context.breaking_change_description: Removal of MUST-forward requirement for baggage headers in async contexts in W3C TC Level 2 draft.
